title: Scalable Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models: Centralized or Decentralized Systems?

defines.name: DMAS
defines.definition: A decentralized multi-agent system where each robot has its own LLM agent and planning proceeds through turn-taking dialogue rounds.

defines.name: CMAS
defines.definition: A centralized multi-agent system where a single LLM generates the next action for all robots.

defines.name: HMAS-1
defines.definition: A hybrid multi-agent system that augments decentralized planning with a central LLM that provides an initial plan to prime the dialogue.

defines.name: HMAS-2
defines.definition: A hybrid multi-agent system that augments centralized planning with robot-local LLM feedback to the central planner.

problem: Existing LLM-based multi-robot planning approaches do not scale well to many agents and long-horizon tasks because coordination complexity and context-window token limits degrade performance.
